artifact: P2 Owner-local preflight enablement and candidate-freeze proposal

overall.one_line_summary: The repository-safe proposal and preflight receipt structure are sound, but stale-state and path-capacity checks are not yet strong enough to prove completion.
strengths: The proposal validates as draft_owner_review and not_adopted with exactly four controls and eight preregistered candidates.
The receipt schema and writer use canonical JSON, SHA-256 self-binding, aggregate-only metadata, and exclusive immutable creation.
The current repository remains unmeasured with all real counters at zero and protected surfaces closed.
weaknesses: A passed receipt is not revalidated against current gate and counter authority, so later canonical state changes can leave a stale pass projected as current.
The store boundary check is one-directional and can accept a store directory that contains a Git worktree.
Free space is summed per store path and can double-count one filesystem or volume.
The focused tests do not cover all required negative and stale-state cases.

strengths: The checks target the requested bindings, gates, counters, stores, and proposal lineage.
weaknesses: Passing focused tests do not cover the full required failure surface.
suggestions: Add one negative test for every named preflight invariant and every stale authority source.

strengths: The receipt exposes explicit check IDs and failure codes.
weaknesses: Current validation does not make a prior pass falsifiable after gate, counter, or artifact state changes.
suggestions: Recompute live authority snapshots during receipt validation and reject stale passes.

strengths: The implementation remains CPU-only, aggregate-only, unmeasured, and final-split closed.
weaknesses: The safe-to-measure projection depends on a receipt whose freshness is not fully proven.
suggestions: Keep passed_pending_owner distinct from execution authorization after freshness repair.

strengths: Profile, envelope, campaign, and proposal hashes are linked coherently.
weaknesses: The projected current state can diverge from the canonical gate and counter state after receipt creation.
suggestions: Bind or recompute every mutable authority used to justify a pass.

strengths: The proposal preserves ambiguity and does not register or hash-lock candidates.
weaknesses: Negative-path evidence is incomplete for the store and stale-state boundary.
suggestions: Retain the proposal as non-scientific engineering evidence until Owner review.

strengths: Canonical schemas and deterministic self-hashes are implemented.
weaknesses: Worktree overlap and same-volume capacity accounting can overstate store safety.
suggestions: Use symmetric path-overlap checks and count free bytes once per filesystem or volume.

findings.evidence_locator: The validator checks the receipt's stored gates and counters but does not reload current decision-ledger, campaign, read-model, or P2 artifact state.
findings.observation: A passed_pending_owner receipt can remain valid after D2/D3 or real candidate/counter state changes outside the campaign and envelope files.
findings.reasoning: The read model may project a stale pass as current readiness, violating fail-closed stale-state behavior.
findings.suggestion: Recompute live gate and counter snapshots during validation and reject a passed receipt when either snapshot differs or is no longer safe.

findings.evidence_locator: outside is calculated only as all(not _path_contains(worktree, store)).
findings.observation: A store path that is a parent of a Git worktree is classified outside even though the paths overlap.
findings.reasoning: The store boundary can include repository content and no longer proves separation from all worktrees.
findings.suggestion: Reject overlap in either direction between each store and every worktree.

findings.evidence_locator: aggregate is the sum of free_space_bytes for both store records.
findings.observation: Two disjoint store paths on one filesystem or volume contribute the same available bytes twice.
findings.reasoning: The aggregate capacity check can pass even when actual available capacity is below the requested threshold.
findings.suggestion: Record a non-path filesystem identity internally and sum available bytes once per unique filesystem or volume.

findings.evidence_locator: The focused suite covers proposal validity, two proposal failures, one passing preflight, store overlap, stale campaign, missing check, and stale commit only.
findings.observation: There are no focused negative tests for missing store, file instead of directory, inside/containing worktree, symlink or junction, unwritable or uncleared sentinel, insufficient free space, stale envelope/profile/gate/counter, immutable overwrite, output escape, or failed-receipt consistency.
findings.reasoning: The explicit comprehensive-negative-test requirement is not proven by the current suite.
findings.suggestion: Add focused tests for every named invariant and verify read-model failure projection for stale receipts.

findings.evidence_locator: The failed branch requires any failed check or failure code but does not require failure_codes to equal the failed check IDs.
findings.observation: A self-hash-valid failed receipt can retain inconsistent diagnostic metadata.
findings.reasoning: This does not promote execution, but weakens the audit trail and stale-failure diagnosis.
findings.suggestion: Require exact sorted equality between failure_codes and failed check IDs and verify aggregate free-space consistency.

questions_for_owner: No new Owner decision is required for these engineering repairs; the five approval items already listed in the candidate proposal remain pending.
